programme.title: Reel History of Britain
programme.desc: Melvyn Bragg is at Osterley Park in Middlesex, the site of the first Home Guard training school. Melvyn looks back to the Second World War and a time when millions of ordinary men were prepared to die for their country as Home Guard recruits.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.sub-title: The Golden Age of Coach Travel
programme.desc: From its early origins in the charabanc, the coach had always been the people's form of transport. Cheaper and more flexible than the train, it allowed those who had travelled little further than their own villages and towns a first heady taste of exploration and freedom. It was a safe capsule on wheels from which to venture out into a wider world.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.sub-title: 2024:John Wilson's American Greats at the Proms
programme.desc: A glittering programme including Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue, which celebrates its centenary this year, plus Barber's Adagio for Strings, recorded live from the Royal Albert Hall with the all-star Sinfonia of London. This concert of scintillating American classics is conducted by audience favourite John Wilson and also includes Copland's ballet Billy the Kid suite and John Adams's Harmonielehre. Georgia Mann presents.

programme.title: The Magic of Dance
programme.sub-title: Out in the Limelight, Home in the Rain
programme.desc: Margot Fonteyn explores the dancer's life. The rigours of ballet class, the rehearsals and preparation, and finally the moment of judgment when it's out in the limelight and on with the performance.

programme.title: Peaky Blinders: Rambert's The Redemption of Thomas Shelby
programme.desc: A personal story unfolds in postwar industrial Birmingham as the Shelby family navigate the decisions that determine their fate, and Tommy is intoxicated by mysterious newcomer Grace.

programme.title: Reputations
programme.desc: The series of historical biographies presents a profile of actor John Wayne. His on-screen bravery and his battle with the cancer that eventually killed him contributed to a heroic public image. But Wayne shirked his country's call to arms in World War Two, endorsed the Hollywood blacklist, fervently supported the war in Vietnam and criticised the civil rights movement.

programme.title: Art on the BBC
programme.desc: Often dismissed as a chocolate box painter, in his day, Constable was a revolutionary. Art historian Rose Balston explores six decades of BBC archives to discover how TV has influenced our understanding of him.

programme.title: Art of America
programme.desc: Andrew Graham-Dixon gets under the skin of the modern American metropolis. Beginning at the Statue of Liberty, he discovers how the ambitions of visionary artists and architects helped America remove itself from the shadow of Europe. In Manhattan, he explores the grimy world of early 20th century painters John Sloan and George Bellows, and visits Stockbridge in Massachusetts to explore Norman Rockwell's oeuvre.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team uncover a danger that humanity is only just waking up to - space weather. They meet the dedicated people working to keep us safe from the very worst that the sun can throw at us.

programme.title: Vienna: Empire, Dynasty and Dream
programme.desc: We follow the Habsburgs' rise to power and discover how Vienna marked Europe's front line in the struggle to defend both Christendom from the Ottomans and the Catholic Church from the Protestant revolutionaries that plotted to destroy it.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.desc: The Supreme Court overturns Muhammad Ali's conviction, validating his refusal to serve in the war in Vietnam. In 1974, Ali outduels Frazier, his greatest rival, in their highly anticipated rematch. But to complete his comeback, he must face the fearsome George Foreman.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.sub-title: Round Four: The Spell Remains, Part 2
programme.desc: Muhammad Ali retired in 1981. In 1984, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. Despite his illness, he continued to travel the world spreading his Islamic faith and became a symbol of peace and hope.
